annotation.title_clean: Conseil d'État, juge des référés, ordonnance du 18 mai 2020, n° 440442 – Surveillance par drones (La Quadrature du Net et autre)
annotation.title_en: Council of State, Summary Judge Order of 18 May 2020, No. 440442 – Drone Surveillance (La Quadrature du Net et al.)
annotation.summary_en: French Conseil d'État urgent-applications order finding that Paris police drone surveillance of COVID-19 lockdown compliance processes personal data under Directive 2016/680 without a prior regulatory authorisation after CNIL opinion, a serious and manifestly unlawful breach of privacy. It orders the State to stop drone surveillance until remedied.
key_provisions_or_claims: Annuls the Paris administrative court's interim order of 5 May 2020.
Drone images are personal data because zoom-equipped drones could identify individuals; the surveillance constitutes processing under Directive 2016/680.
Processing without a regulatory text authorised after CNIL opinion (art. 31, Law of 1978) is a serious, manifestly unlawful breach of privacy.
Orders the State to cease drone surveillance until a regulatory text is adopted or drones are technically unable to identify people.
The State must pay €3,000 to each applicant.
